title: Volunteer Success Program — a 120-hour commitment

audience.original: Ages 12–30. Since October 1, 2026, volunteers must commit to completing at least 120 hours.
restrictions: Placement is arranged by the provider; joining is not a guaranteed role.
A minimum 120-hour commitment is required, exceeding the standard Ontario school requirement.
Access to a computer and internet is required by the provider.
Virtual volunteering requires at least 10 hours each month, alongside the overall 120-hour commitment.
Camp counsellor-in-training roles require age 14 or older; general programme age does not establish role eligibility.
audience.residency: Must reside in Canada throughout the volunteer period.

cost.original: The provider describes this programme as completely free.

availability.original: Current page invites intake applications and states it is accepting volunteers who can commit to at least 120 hours.

commitmentOriginal: At least 120 hours overall; the virtual programme also states a minimum 10 hours per month. Confirm tasks, schedule, placement-specific conditions and school eligibility before committing. Provider selection is required; availability is not a shift confirmation.

title: Youth for Entrepreneurship

audience.original: Youth ages 15–24. Virtual across Canada; in-person programming in Ontario and Newfoundland and Labrador.

cost.original: The provider states the programme is free.

availability.original: Programme is described, but this page does not establish a current session date or available place. Ask the provider.

commitmentOriginal: Workshops and mentorship about starting projects and businesses. Confirm the next session and local arrangements.

title: Black Achievers Mentorship Program

audience.original: Black youth in high school in the Greater Toronto Area.
restrictions: For Black high-school students. GTA does not infer a visitor's identity.

cost.original: The provider states the programme is free.

availability.original: Current intake dates and places are not established on this programme overview. Confirm with the provider.

commitmentOriginal: Mentoring and workshops for school and career planning.

title: Newcomer Youth Leadership Development

audience.original: Newcomer youth ages 13–24 living in the Greater Toronto Area.
restrictions: For newcomer youth; confirm the provider's eligibility conditions.

cost.original: The provider states the programme is free.

availability.original: Programme overview does not establish current session availability. Confirm with the provider.

commitmentOriginal: Group activities developing leadership and community connections. Attending is not automatically a volunteer role or school credit.

title: Blueprint 2027 — engineering enrichment

audience.original: Canadian citizens or permanent residents who identify as Black and are in Grades 10 or 11 in the 2026–2027 academic year.
audience.residency: Canadian citizenship or permanent residency required
restrictions: For students who identify as Black; GTA does not infer identity.

cost.original: Tuition is free. Travel, accommodation and lunches/snacks are not included. Bring your own lunch or buy it; confirm necessary expenses and possible travel support.

requiredCosts.description: Travel to the in-person programme and accommodation if needed. Lunches/snacks are not supplied; bring your own or buy them. Necessary costs depend on circumstances.

availability.original: Applications open November 2, 2026 at 9:00am. Summer programme runs July 5–30, 2027, followed by school-year engagement. Application deadline: March 29, 2027; no exact closing time is stated.

commitmentOriginal: Four summer weeks plus later school-year engagement. This is learning, not a volunteer placement; no school volunteer hours are promised.

title: Plan for scholarships, bursaries and student aid

audience.original: Planning to study at college, university or an apprenticeship after high school. Each funding programme has its own eligibility.

cost.original: Official information resource, not a particular award or a promise of funding.

availability.original: This is guidance, not an open scholarship listing. Check each award's own conditions and dates.

commitmentOriginal: Compare scholarships and bursaries with repayable loans. Ask your school or chosen institution about its awards; GTA does not assess financial-aid eligibility.

title: Find youth-suitable roles with Volunteer Toronto

audience.original: Guidance for high-school volunteers, with links to its opportunity search. Each role has its own age and school requirements.

cost.original: Directory only. Check costs and requirements for the individual role; no free opening is asserted.

availability.original: This page is a place to look, not a confirmed vacancy.

audience.original: Library volunteering information, including youth participation from age 14. Intake, selection and role requirements must be checked with the library.
restrictions: Provider requires an account, interview, vulnerable-sector check and orientation. Confirm age-specific check arrangements before applying.

cost.original: The page lists a $35 vulnerable-sector-check charge in its adult guidance. Confirm the check cost and any age-specific conditions with the library; this is not a verified zero-cost role.

requiredCosts.description: Required vulnerable-sector check; page lists a $35 charge in adult guidance. Confirm the fee applicable to you.

availability.original: This page is a place to look, not a confirmed vacancy.

title: Understand your school community-involvement requirements

audience.original: Ontario high-school students. Confirm your own graduation requirements and planned activity with your school.

cost.original: Official guidance, not a volunteer placement.

availability.original: Information resource; it does not offer a role or approve an activity.

commitmentOriginal: Ontario generally requires 40 community-involvement hours for the diploma. Students can start in the summer before Grade 9. Get school confirmation before starting; keep the required school record and any required parent or guardian sign-off. Paid work, course requirements and ordinary chores do not automatically qualify. GTA only records actual completed time and cannot certify school credit.
